faq.q: How many baby teeth do we have?
faq.a: Children have 20 baby teeth, also called milk teeth or primary teeth. Most have all of them by about age three.
asks: How many milk teeth do children have?

faq.q: Where do adult teeth come from?
faq.a: Adult teeth develop inside the jawbone from tooth buds that form before and soon after birth. They grow slowly, hidden beneath or behind the baby teeth, until they are ready to come through.
asks: Are adult teeth already in the jaw?

faq.q: Why do baby teeth get wobbly?
faq.a: As the adult tooth grows, cells called odontoclasts dissolve the baby tooth's root. With less and less root holding it in the gum, the tooth becomes loose and wobbles.
asks: Why does a tooth come loose?
Where does the root of a baby tooth go?

faq.q: How many adult teeth do people have?
faq.a: Adults can have up to 32 permanent teeth, including four wisdom teeth at the back, which often come through in the late teens or twenties, or sometimes not at all.
asks: How many teeth do adults have?

faq.q: Why do we need baby teeth at all?
faq.a: Baby teeth let young children chew and speak, and they hold space in the jaw for the adult teeth. A small child's jaw is too small for full-sized adult teeth.
asks: Why not grow adult teeth first?

facts: Children have 20 baby teeth; adults can have up to 32 permanent teeth.
Children usually start losing baby teeth at around age 6.
